subject: Chemistry
description: Alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, aromatic; petroleum + natural gas

questions.explanation: HYDROCARBONS = compounds of ONLY C + H. Three families: ALKANES (C_nH_(2n+2); single bonds, saturated; methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆, propane C₃H₈, butane C₄H₁₀); ALKENES (C_nH_(2n); 1 double bond, unsaturated; ethene C₂H₄, propene C₃H₆); ALKYNES (C_nH_(2n−2); 1 triple bond; ethyne / acetylene C₂H₂). Plus AROMATICS (with benzene-ring; benzene C₆H₆, toluene). Sources: PETROLEUM (crude oil), NATURAL GAS, COAL.

questions.stem: METHANE (CH₄), the main component of NATURAL GAS, is also a:
questions.explanation: METHANE (CH₄) — simplest hydrocarbon (1 C + 4 H). Major natural gas component (~80-95%). GREENHOUSE GAS — 25-86× more potent than CO₂ over 100/20 years. Sources of CH₄ emissions: cattle (enteric fermentation), rice paddies, landfills, oil + gas leaks, melting permafrost (a feedback risk). LIGHTER than air. Burns to give CO₂ + H₂O + heat. India's Bharat Stage VI norms address some hydrocarbon emissions. Distractor 4 — methane is LIGHTER than air (escapes upward; useful: gas leaks rise to ceiling).

questions.explanation: ETHENE (ethylene): CH₂=CH₂. C=C double bond + 4 C-H bonds. ALKENE family: CₙH₂ₙ. Used: (1) PLANT HORMONE — ripens fruit (Banana ripening, mango ripening with ethylene-releasing chemicals like ethrel — illegal in many places, calcium carbide also used illegally). (2) POLYMERIZATION → POLYTHENE / POLYETHYLENE (most common plastic — bags, bottles); (3) precursor in industrial chemistry. ETHYNE (ACETYLENE) C₂H₂ — TRIPLE bond; oxy-acetylene welding burns very hot.

questions.stem: BENZENE (C₆H₆), discovered by Faraday in 1825, is:

options.option_text: Alicyclic, with single bonds in the ring
Inorganic salt, with ionic bonding only

questions.explanation: BENZENE (C₆H₆) — prototypical AROMATIC compound: 6 carbons in planar HEXAGONAL ring; alternating single + double bonds (Kekulé structure 1865) — but actually 6 DELOCALISED π-electrons spread evenly over the ring (= AROMATICITY). Hückel's rule: aromatic if (4n+2) π electrons (n=1 for benzene → 6). Stable, distinctive 'aromatic' smell (originally named for fragrance). CARCINOGENIC. Found in petrol, cigarette smoke. Used in: making styrene, phenol, plastics, drugs, dyes. AROMATIC family includes: TOLUENE (methyl-benzene), XYLENE, NAPHTHALENE (mothballs).

questions.stem: LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas, used as cooking fuel) is mainly a mixture of:
questions.explanation: LPG = mostly PROPANE (C₃H₈) + BUTANE (C₄H₁₀); some ratio depends on country (India winter formulation different from summer). Distinctive smell = ETHYL MERCAPTAN (added as warning of leaks; LPG itself is odourless). Stored under PRESSURE as LIQUID in cylinder; vaporises when released. CNG (Compressed Natural Gas — used in CNG vehicles): mainly METHANE (~95%). PNG (Piped Natural Gas — household + commercial): same as CNG. India produces LPG from refineries + imports; PMUY (Ujjwala) gave free LPG connection to ~10 crore poor households.

questions.stem: PETROLEUM (crude oil) is separated into useful fractions by:
questions.explanation: FRACTIONAL DISTILLATION at petroleum refineries. Crude oil heated; vapour rises in tall fractionating column; different fractions condense at different heights based on BOILING POINT. From bottom (heaviest) to top (lightest): bitumen / asphalt → fuel oil → diesel → kerosene → naphtha → petrol/gasoline → LPG → refinery gas. Each fraction further refined. India's major refineries: Reliance Jamnagar (world's largest), IOC's Mathura + Panipat + Gujarat, BPCL Mumbai, HPCL Visakhapatnam.

questions.stem: POLYTHENE (plastic bags) is made by polymerising:
questions.explanation: POLYTHENE / POLYETHYLENE — long-chain polymer of ethene monomers: nCH₂=CH₂ → −(CH₂−CH₂)ₙ−. Two main types: LDPE (Low-Density PE — branched chains; soft, flexible — plastic bags, squeeze bottles); HDPE (High-Density PE — linear chains; harder — bottles, pipes, crates). World's most produced plastic. ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUE: doesn't biodegrade easily; plastic pollution. Many states banned single-use plastic bags. Other common plastics: PVC (polyvinyl chloride — pipes), PS (polystyrene — packaging), PP (polypropylene — bottle caps, ropes), PET (polyethylene terephthalate — water bottles), PTFE (Teflon — non-stick coating).
